answer: Sybil resistance makes identities costly to duplicate, not merely numerous. A new agent key posts a slashable escrow bond, and its weight scales only with peer-attested work, so a fresh key starts at zero. Admission pricing rises with registry load, so one clone costs its bond plus entry, and a thousand clones multiply that while collateral stays frozen and is slashed on cheating. Honest agents recover the cost through fees; attackers do not. The barrier is a karst, not thin timber, and fees act as a prism splitting one cheap attempt into a thousand unbudgetable ones.
